extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, visual journalists, filmmakers and entrants to the NPPA Best of Photojournalism contest
extracted.subtask_description: Ethical and technical rules for capturing, editing, and presenting still and video work submitted to the NPPA Best of Photojournalism competition, emphasizing accuracy, non-manipulation, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be accurate and comprehensive in representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be accurate and comprehensive in the representation of subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core NPPA Code of Ethics requirement applied to all entries; underpins making/capturing and post-production rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist manipulation by staged photo opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist being manipulated by staged photo opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should avoid allowing others to stage or direct images in ways that compromise authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide context; avoid stereotyping and bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Be complete and provide context when photographing or recording subjects. Avoid stereotyping individuals and groups. Recognize and work to avoid presenting one's own biases in the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes contextual captions, selection of images, and editorial choices that prevent misleading impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and dignity for subjects; special consideration for vulnerable people
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat all subjects with respect and dignity. Give special consideration to vulnerable subjects and compassion to victims of crime or tragedy. Intrude on private moments of grief only when the public has an overriding and justifiable need to see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply heightened judgment before photographing or publishing images of victims or vulnerable populations; weigh public interest against intrusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not alter or influence events while photographing
rubrics_metrics.description: While photographing subjects do not intentionally contribute to, alter, or seek to alter or influence events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers must remain observers, not participants or instigators of the scene being captured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing must maintain integrity of content and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing should maintain the integrity of the photographic images' content and context. Do not manipulate images or add or alter sound in any way that can mislead viewers or misrepresent subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers still-image edits and audio/video editing; any edit that changes meaning or misrepresents subjects is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay or materially reward sources/subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not pay sources or subjects or reward them materially for information or participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary or material inducements that influence coverage are disallowed for entrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid accepting gifts/favors that influence coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept gifts, favors, or compensation from those who might seek to influence coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain independence and avoid conflicts of interest that could undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not sabotage other journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not intentionally sabotage the efforts of other journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional conduct includes not undermining colleagues' reporting or access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professional behavior; no harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not engage in harassing behavior of colleagues, subordinates or subjects and maintain the highest standards of behavior in all professional interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants are expected to uphold workplace- and public-facing standards of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend access and public conduct of public business
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to ensure that the public's business is conducted in public. Defend the rights of access for all journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy for transparent public institutions and defending reporters' access rights are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop unique vision through study
rubrics_metrics.description: Think proactively, as a student of psychology, sociology, politics and art to develop a unique vision and presentation. Work with a voracious appetite for current events and contemporary visual media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspiration to combine technical skill with intellectual context to produce informed visual storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek diversity of viewpoints and show unnoticed points of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive for total and unrestricted access to subjects, recommend alternatives to shallow or rushed opportunities, seek a diversity of viewpoints, and work to show unpopular or unnoticed points of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages thorough reporting and inclusion of multiple perspectives to avoid narrow or biased narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest in outside involvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid political, civic and business involvements or other employment that compromise or give the appearance of compromising one's own journalistic independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal affiliations that could be seen as compromising objectivity should be avoided or disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be unobtrusive and humble; respect the photographic moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive to be unobtrusive and humble in dealing with subjects. Respect the integrity of the photographic moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographers should minimize interference and preserve authentic moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek counsel when unsure and continuously study ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Strive by example and influence to maintain the spirit and high standards expressed in this code. When confronted with situations in which the proper action is not clear, seek the counsel of those who exhibit the highest standards of the profession. Visual journalists should continuously study their craft and the ethics that guide it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult mentors/peers on difficult ethical decisions and pursue ongoing ethics and craft education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add objects when making/capturing the image
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographers must not intentionally alter the scene they capture: You must not add objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits introducing props, items or elements into a scene to change its content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not move or remove objects when making/capturing the image
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographers must not intentionally alter the scene they capture: You must not move/take away objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rearranging or removing elements from the scene to improve composition or narrative is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not 'stage' situations when making/capturing the image
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographers must not intentionally alter the scene they capture: You must not 'stage' situations – meaning you must not deliberately arrange objects, subjects or situations that are not already occurring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants may not direct subjects or orchestrate events to simulate a real occurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not 'set-up' scenes that do not exist
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not 'set-up' situations – meaning you must not deliberately create a situation that does not exist. For example, bringing disparate characters together in a place they would not be, giving or directing subjects to wear particular clothing, or creating or altering a scene by painting, adding objects, or people that aren’t normally in that location or occur in that location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit examples clarify that assembling people, staging clothing/props, or altering locations is disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not ask subjects to re-enact past actions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not ask your subject to re-enact actions or scenes that occurred in the past in order to make a photograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-enactments that present themselves as documentary events are not allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrait construction allowed only if labeled as portrait
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits have different rules. Portraits can be constructed as long as they are identified as portraits in the captions. They must not be made to look like they are naturally occurring events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructed/staged portraits are acceptable when transparently captioned as portraits; they must not be presented as documentary candids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal post-processing allowed (toning/color correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-processing, in and of itself, is not manipulation as long as it is within normal limits of toning and color correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine exposure, white balance, contrast and minor tonal adjustments are permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic color changes that alter original scene are manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of post-processing that count as manipulation: Dramatic changes in color that alter the original color of the scene. For example, changing a gray sky to blue. Color correcting sensor/white balance issues from incorrect camera settings is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Altering a scene's actual color relationship to change mood or meaning is prohibited; color correction for technical errors is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dodging/burning and adjustments that significantly alter content are manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes made by dodging or burning, adjustments to brightness, contrast, color, saturation, sharpening or clarity that significantly alter content by obscuring, enhancing or diminishing elements in the photograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edits that materially change which elements are visible or emphasized (thus changing meaning) are disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add/move/remove people or objects in post-production; cloning restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Just like during the making/capturing of an image you may not add, move, remove any objects or persons. You may only use the cloning tool – or any other tool – to remove dust spots on the image created by the lens, the camera sensor or dust from scanning physical negatives. You may NOT use the cloning tool – or any other tool – to extend the photograph or expand the canvas of the photograph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cloning is limited to sensor/dust cleanup; no compositing, removal of subjects, or canvas extension is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Altering audio/video sequencing to change meaning is manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Altering the sequencing of an audio or video recording so as to change the meaning of someone’s statement or apparent actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cuts, reordering or edits that produce a false narrative or misattributed meaning are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges may request camera-original images; potential disqualification
rubrics_metrics.description: If the judges have any questions regarding any possible image manipulation in post processing, entrants will be required to submit images as recorded by the camera. The judges will have a private conversation regarding the entry and the entry may be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should preserve and be ready to provide original/RAW files and edit metadata to verify authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: No payment from parties with a commercial stake; no branded content
rubrics_metrics.description: Filmmakers and photographers cannot be paid by anyone with a commercial stake in the story, and no branded content will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercially funded or sponsored content that could create bias is ineligible for contest entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candid scenes must not be set up; re-creations must be labeled
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should honor the viewer's trust, and under no circumstances should scenes depicted as candid be set up, directed or controlled in any way. Any re-creations of scenes to illustrate events in the past must be clearly marked as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is required for any staged or recreated material; presenting a staged scene as candid is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use special effects and music sparingly; do not alter truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Special effects and music should be used sparingly and not alter the truthfulness of the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio/visual enhancements that change the perceived reality or emotional framing to the point of misrepresentation are discouraged.
